data.text: Correction: research run R20261022-031116 compared candidates against a SPY baseline that was bought in 2007, tripped the 35% drawdown breaker in 2008 and sat in cash, so its reference CAGR was 0%. From the next run on, the baseline is bought at the start of the measured window (2010-08 onward: CAGR 14.4%, max DD 33.7%). Separately, 20 ML candidates in that run errored on an all-empty feature (high-yield spread, unavailable without FRED); fixed. The run's candidate records stay in the log and count toward the multiple-testing total.

Daily runs on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 failed before marking any book (price merge rejected timezone-aware dates from the source; fixed). The first catch-up run fills both days in order: each decision uses only data through its decision date and fills at the next open, so no future information is used, but these two days were recorded after the fact rather than on the evening they occurred.

known_limitations: Survivorship bias: free listing sources contain only currently listed securities, so the research and holdout periods exclude companies that were delisted, acquired or went bankrupt before system init. Backtest returns are biased upward by an unknown amount (published estimates for US equities range from roughly 1 to 4 percent a year). From init onward, delisted tickers are retained.
Bid-ask spreads are modeled (1 + 50/sqrt(ADV $M) bps, capped at 25) because free historical quote data does not exist; actual spreads in stressed markets were wider.

Fundamentals use the first-reported value for each fiscal period (no restatements) and are available the trading day after the SEC filing date. Companies that file under non-us-gaap taxonomies (many foreign filers) have sparse fundamentals.
Yahoo Finance is an unofficial source and can rate-limit or change format; Stooq is the fallback.
Historical index membership, short interest, analyst estimates, options data and intraday prices are not available from free sources and are not used.
Cash earns 0% in the paper book (conservative versus a money-market sweep).
